title.en: There is, there are: a lot of stars
title.sl: There is, there are: je, so
title.it: There is, there are: c'è, ci sono
title.de: There is, there are: es gibt

rule.en:
To say that something exists or is somewhere, English starts with **there**: **there is** (short **there's**) + one thing or something you can't count, **there are** + more than one: **There's a tent by the pond.** **There's some milk.** **There are a lot of stars tonight.**

The negative is **there isn't** / **there aren't**, often with any: **There isn't any bread.** **There aren't any clouds.** A question turns it round: **Is there a shop in the village?** **Are there any fish in the tarn?** Short answers: **Yes, there is.** / **No, there aren't.**

The past: **there was**, **there were**: **There were fifty sheep on the fell.**

Don't mix it up with **it is**: there is says that something is there, it is says what it is like: **There's a bridge. It's very old.**
rule.sl:
Ko povemo, da nekaj obstaja ali je nekje, angleščina začne s **there**: **there is** (kratko **there's**) + ena stvar ali nekaj neštevnega, **there are** + več stvari: **There's a tent by the pond.** (Ob ribniku je šotor.) **There's some milk.** **There are a lot of stars tonight.** (Nocoj je veliko zvezd.)

Slovenščina tu reče le je ali so; angleščina ne more začeti z *Is a tent* ali *Are many stars*, there je obvezen.

Zanikanje je **there isn't** / **there aren't**, pogosto z any: **There isn't any bread.** (Kruha ni.) **There aren't any clouds.** Vprašanje obrne vrstni red: **Is there a shop in the village?** (Je v vasi trgovina?) **Are there any fish in the tarn?** Kratki odgovori: **Yes, there is.** / **No, there aren't.**

V pretekliku: **there was**, **there were**: **There were fifty sheep on the fell.** (Na hribu je bilo petdeset ovc.)

Ne zamenjaj z **it is**: there is pove, da nekaj je, it is pove, kakšno je: **There's a bridge. It's very old.** (Tam je most. Zelo star je.)
rule.it:
Per dire che una cosa c'è, l'inglese ha **there is** e **there are**, proprio come c'è e ci sono: **there is** (breve **there's**) + una cosa sola o un nome non numerabile, **there are** + più cose: **There's a tent by the pond.** (C'è una tenda vicino allo stagno.) **There's some milk.** **There are a lot of stars tonight.** (Stasera ci sono tante stelle.)

La negazione è **there isn't** / **there aren't**, spesso con any: **There isn't any bread.** (Non c'è pane.) **There aren't any clouds.** Nella domanda si inverte: **Is there a shop in the village?** (C'è un negozio in paese?) **Are there any fish in the tarn?** Risposte brevi: **Yes, there is.** / **No, there aren't.**

Al passato: **there was**, **there were** (c'era, c'erano): **There were fifty sheep on the fell.**

Non confonderlo con **it is**: there is dice che una cosa c'è, it is dice com'è: **There's a bridge. It's very old.** (C'è un ponte. È molto vecchio.)
rule.de:
Um zu sagen, dass etwas da ist oder existiert, beginnt das Englische mit **there**: **there is** (kurz **there's**) + eine Sache oder etwas Unzählbares, **there are** + mehrere: **There's a tent by the pond.** (Am Teich steht ein Zelt.) **There's some milk.** **There are a lot of stars tonight.** (Heute Nacht sind viele Sterne am Himmel.)

Anders als *es gibt*, das immer gleich bleibt, richtet sich das Verb nach der Zahl: **is** für eins, **are** für mehrere. Und nie *It gives*.

Die Verneinung ist **there isn't** / **there aren't**, oft mit any: **There isn't any bread.** (Es gibt kein Brot.) **There aren't any clouds.** Die Frage dreht es um: **Is there a shop in the village?** (Gibt es im Dorf einen Laden?) **Are there any fish in the tarn?** Kurze Antworten: **Yes, there is.** / **No, there aren't.**

In der Vergangenheit: **there was**, **there were**: **There were fifty sheep on the fell.**

Nicht verwechseln mit **it is**: there is sagt, dass etwas da ist, it is sagt, wie es ist: **There's a bridge. It's very old.** (Da ist eine Brücke. Sie ist sehr alt.)

examples.sl: Nocoj je na nebu veliko zvezd.
examples.de: Heute Nacht sind viele Sterne am Himmel.

examples.en: There's a tent by the pond.
examples.it: C'è una tenda vicino allo stagno.

examples.en: Is there a shop in the village? — Yes, there is.
examples.sl: Je v vasi trgovina? — Ja, je.
examples.it: C'è un negozio in paese? — Sì, c'è.
examples.de: Gibt es im Dorf einen Laden? — Ja.

note.en: The question turns it round: Is there …? Short answer: Yes, there is.
note.sl: Vprašanje obrne red: Is there …? Kratki odgovor: Yes, there is.
note.it: La domanda si inverte: Is there …? Risposta breve: Yes, there is.
note.de: Die Frage dreht es um: Is there …? Kurzantwort: Yes, there is.

examples.en: Are there any fish in the tarn?

note.en: fish is plural here, so are.
note.sl: fish je tu množina, zato are.
note.it: fish qui è plurale, quindi are.
note.de: fish ist hier Plural, also are.

examples.en: There isn't any bread, but there's some honey.
examples.sl: Kruha ni, je pa nekaj medu.
examples.it: Non c'è pane, ma c'è un po' di miele.
examples.de: Es gibt kein Brot, aber etwas Honig.

examples.en: There's an old bridge over the beck. It's made of stone.
examples.sl: Čez potok vodi star most. Narejen je iz kamna.
examples.it: Sul ruscello c'è un vecchio ponte. È di pietra.
examples.de: Über den Bach führt eine alte Brücke. Sie ist aus Stein.

note.en: there's: something is there; it's: what it is like.
note.sl: there's: nekaj tam je; it's: kakšno je.
note.it: there's: una cosa c'è; it's: com'è.
note.de: there's: etwas ist da; it's: wie es ist.

examples.en: There were fifty sheep on the fell.
examples.sl: Na hribu je bilo petdeset ovc.
examples.de: Auf dem Berg waren fünfzig Schafe.
